{"content": "1|---
2|name: debateai-graph-spine
3|title: DebateAI Graph Spine v2
4|version: 3.0.0
5|supersedes: debateai-heartbeat-protocol (pre-3.0.0), heartbeat-protocol-lite, debateai-kanban-heartbeat-review-loop
6|---
7|
8|# DebateAI Graph Spine v2
9|
10|This is the single normative document for DebateAI multi-agent work — the graph
11|of nodes, edges, routers, and typed state. Hermes, Codex, Claude, and Grok load
12|this spine first, then their own thin node contract. Where an older per-agent
13|skill or the Hermes AppData FULL body disagrees with this spine, this spine wins;
14|those documents are demoted to implementation notes.
15|
16|## Table of contents
17|
18|1. Pillars
19|2. State contract
20|3. Node contracts index
21|4. Launch packet contract
22|5. Routers: Claude-Router and Hermes-Verifier
23|6. Stage numbering (H0–H9)
24|7. Edges, diamonds, and feedback edges
25|8. Marker vocabulary (union)
26|9. Review-lane applicability
27|10. Convergence and batched-approval laws
28|11. Preserved laws (verbatim)
29|12. Glossary
30|
31|## 1. Pillars
32|
33|The harness is a graph built on four pillars. Every rule in this spine serves one
34|of them.
35|
36|- **Node** — a bounded job with a file contract and no graph knowledge. A node
37|  reads its own ticket state and its declared upstream artifacts; it never reads
38|  the whole board or a mission route.
39|- **Edge** — a data-flow, not an "and then". An edge carries a named artifact or
40|  a typed verdict from one node to the next. Status is not a message; edges signal
41|  through the typed state block and handoff markers.
42|- **Router** — dispatches, does no work. The router reads typed state, picks the
43|  next edge, and writes only routing metadata. Content judgment belongs to a
44|  verifier, never to the router (§5).
45|- **State** — one typed ticket-state object per ticket (§2). All other carriers
46|  (live files, host task lists) are read-only projections regenerated from it.
47|
48|Operating model: **V prompts exactly one node (H0 intake).** Everything else
49|reaches V only through the V DECISIONS PACKET (§10) or final acceptance. Routine
50|routing and review communication live in ticket comments, never in V's inbox.
51|
52|```text
53|V → Claude-Router (intake H0 only)
54|Claude-Router → assignment, status, epoch, route
55|Hermes-Verifier → evidence verdicts
56|Codex → sole coding worker while the current model law is active
57|Claude/Grok → planning-artifact workers and independent read-only reviewers
58|Kanban → durable shared state (the typed state block is its first comment)
59|```
60|
61|## Operating model
62|
63|```text
64|V → Hermes cockpit
65|Hermes → tickets, dependencies, comments, review routing, human-review packets, Done/Blocked
66|Codex → sole coding worker while the current model law is active
67|Claude/Grok → planning-artifact workers and independent read-only reviewers
68|Kanban → durable shared state
69|```
70|
71|V is interrupted ONLY for an **IMPORTANT OPERATION** or final acceptance.
72|The IMPORTANT OPERATIONS are, exactly: provider/model spend or external calls;
73|secrets/auth; product/live DB or product-data writes; any deletion; destructive
74|filesystem/Git/history; commit/push/merge/release/branch/worktree operations;
75|architecture or scope expansion; reconstructed-evidence acceptance/waiver; and
76|final human/product acceptance. Anything outside this list is not an important
77|operation and is handled inside Hermes and the ticket comments, never by
78|interrupting V. Routine routing and review communication belong in ticket comments.
79|
80|### The One-Prompt Machine law
81|
82|A mission starts with exactly ONE V prompt at REQUIREMENTS (H0). From that moment
83|the machine runs itself: V never relays prompts, pastes agent output, or presses
84|Resume. Exactly three V-facing surfaces exist for the entire mission:
85|
86|1. DESIGN QUESTIONS: only the REQUIREMENTS node (H0 intake) and the ARCHITECTURE
87|   nodes (planning diamond C2/H2/G3/H3/C4) may address questions or steering
88|   requests to V directly, and only during design. No implementation, QA, watcher,
89|   or worker node ever addresses V.
90|2. IMPORTANT-OPERATION DECISIONS: from ANY node, a decision on the IMPORTANT
91|   OPERATIONS list above (database deletion, data manipulation, security/auth,
92|   provider spend, destructive git/filesystem, architecture or scope expansion,
93|   reconstructed evidence, waiver) reaches V exclusively as a row in the batched
94|   V DECISIONS PACKET. Cap-triggered V STEERING REQUIRED escalations
95|   (rework_round cap, chatter breaker, reset ceiling) travel the same way.
96|3. FINAL ACCEPTANCE (H9).
97|
98|Any other V-facing message is a protocol violation: Claude-Router intercepts it
99|and re-routes it as a design question (if its origin is REQUIREMENTS/ARCHITECTURE),
100|a packet row (if it is an important operation or cap escalation), or an ordinary
101|ticket comment (everything else).
102|
103|## Default full-mode operation and V touchpoints
104|
105|Default operation is FULL mode: Claude (the Main Orchestrator, the Claude-Router
106|seat, ruling R1) launches and holds the agent sessions (managed PTYs or scripted
107|CLI bridges), routes every agent on typed state, and drives them through ticket
108|comments; Hermes-Verifier holds Kanban board custody and crafting, mutates the
109|board, and runs verification and Manual QA.
110|V does not paste prompts, relay output, or press Resume in full mode.
111|
112|V is touched exactly through the three One-Prompt Machine surfaces (law above):
113|
114|1. Intake and design questions: V states the mission at H0 with the single
115|   mission prompt; during design, the REQUIREMENTS and ARCHITECTURE nodes (and
116|   only those) may ask V questions or request steering. Claude-Router classifies
117|   and sets `risk_tier` at intake.
118|2. V DECISIONS PACKETS: Claude-Router batches V-owned gates (the named-category
119|   filter decides what qualifies) from Hermes-Verifier's verdicts and blocks, and
120|   flushes one consolidated packet per the flush thresholds (>=3 pending, or any
121|   pending >4h, or a lane frozen, or V asks). This includes the per-mission
122|   worktree lane-plan approval submitted at H6.
123|3. Final acceptance: V performs the final human/product acceptance at the
124|   mission's closure gate.
125|
126|Everything else — routing (Claude-Router), review and board custody
127|(Hermes-Verifier), rework, successor dispatch — stays inside the orchestrator /
128|verifier loop and the ticket comments. Reducing V touchpoints never removes a
129|safety gate: a frozen loop (rework cap, chatter breaker, reset ceiling) escalates
130|into the V DECISIONS PACKET; it never auto-approves.
131|
132|## Orchestrator outage fallback (ruling R3)
133|
134|If the Claude (Main Orchestrator) session is down,
135|the Architecture-responsible agent communicates directly with the humans ("us" = anyone using the harness)
136|until the orchestrator is restored. This is legal WITHOUT creating a new V-facing
137|surface: ARCHITECTURE already holds design-question authority under the One-Prompt
138|Machine law (surface (a)), so the outage relay rides an existing authorized
139|channel. It is a temporary continuity measure, recorded on the affected tickets;
140|no other loop gains a human-facing channel, and every spine law still binds.
141|
142|## Degraded-hardware V-relay fallback
143|
144|Full mode is the default. Only when the machine cannot host the orchestrator's
145|managed agent sessions at all, the orchestrator falls back to V-as-relay:
146|
147|- Claude-Router emits exactly one copy-paste prompt for the next required
148|  agent/stage.
149|- V pastes it into the external agent and returns the artifact/handoff.
150|- Hermes-Verifier reviews, records the gate, and Claude-Router supplies the next
151|  single prompt.
152|
153|This is a TRANSPORT fallback only. Every law in this spine still binds:
154|independent review, no self-Done, the `rework_round` cap, the chatter breaker,
155|`risk_tier` routing, and the IMPORTANT OPERATIONS gates. Set the semaphore
156|`max_concurrent_heavy: 1` on constrained hardware. V-relay is never the default
157|and is recorded explicitly on the ticket whenever used.
158|
159|## 2. State contract
160|
161|Every ticket carries exactly one canonical typed state object. It is the single
162|source of truth for routing; every other carrier (`.hermes/live/` files, host
163|task lists, watcher fingerprints, compaction checkpoints) is a read-only
164|projection regenerated from it.
165|
166|Storage rule: if Kanban exposes native custom fields, the state object lives in
167|those fields. If it does not, the state object is written as the ticket's FIRST
168|comment and is updated **by replacement** of that one comment — never appended,
169|never smeared across the thread, never duplicated in a later comment.
170|
171|```yaml
172|state:
173|  ticket: <id>
174|  risk_tier: low | medium | high            # set ONCE at intake/H6; drives routing deterministically
175|  status: queued | ready | working
176|        | waiting_review | waiting_hermes | waiting_product_proof
177|        | waiting_human | waiting_dependency | waiting_resource
178|        | failed_tooling | changes_requested | done | archived
179|  owner: { agent: codex|claude|grok, session: <id> }
180|  contract:
181|    allowed: [...]
182|    readonly: [...]
183|    forbidden: all_others
184|    verification: [...]
185|    human_review: yes|no
186|  worktree: { path: <.worktrees/lane-x>, branch: <b>, merge_status: none|pending|merged }
187|  authority_epoch: <int>                     # monotonic; V/cockpit-only writer
188|  rework_round: <int>                        # convergence counter; cap = 3
189|  wakes_since_transition: <int>              # chatter counter
190|  waiting_since: <timestamp>                 # every waiting_* status carries it
191|  escalation_target: hermes | v_packet       # every waiting_* status carries it
192|  self_unblock_enabled: false                # V-toggled worker-self-unblock capability; default false
193|  comments_read_through: <cursor>
194|```
195|
196|The Codex worker-self-unblock exception (Blocked -> In Progress recovery on the
197|worker's own active card) exists ONLY when `self_unblock_enabled: true`, which only V
198|sets, per-ticket. Default is `false`: with it false, no worker may self-recover a
199|Blocked card; an important-operation, human, safety, or product gate is never
200|self-cleared regardless of this flag.
201|
202|The `status` enum replaces the overloaded word `blocked`. A ticket status is
203|never a bare `blocked`; every former "blocked" meaning maps to a specific
204|`waiting_*` status (or `changes_requested`/`failed_tooling`) per the mapping
205|table in "## Blocked format". Which node may read or write which field is
206|declared per node in each agent adapter; `risk_tier` and `authority_epoch` are
207|Hermes/cockpit-only writes.
208|
209|This block is **forward-compatible**: it lists the twelve top-level fields
210|installed now, and later phases MAY append additional additive fields without
211|breaking earlier readers (which key only on the fields present). Two such fields
212|are added downstream — `planning_tier` (planning-chain depth `0|1|2`, added by
213|Phase 4 Task 4.2, distinct from `risk_tier`) and `self_unblock_enabled`
214|(V-toggled worker-self-unblock capability, default `false`, added by Phase 3
215|Task 3.11). Do not pre-add them here; they are named only so the schema is known
216|to be open for additive extension.
217|
218|## 3. Node contracts index
219|
220|Each agent loads this spine, then exactly one thin node contract. A node contract
221|declares the node's role, its state reads/writes, and its markers. Nothing else.
222|
223|```text
224|Codex node contract   → DebateV2/apps/dialectical-engine/.codex/skills/heartbeat-protocol/SKILL.md
225|                        (also .agents/skills/heartbeat-protocol/SKILL.md)
226|Claude node contract  → DebateV2/apps/dialectical-engine/.claude/skills/heartbeat-protocol/SKILL.md
227|Grok node contract    → DebateV2/apps/dialectical-engine/.grok/skills/heartbeat-protocol/SKILL.md
228|Hermes node contract  → DebateV2/apps/dialectical-engine/.hermes/skills/heartbeat-protocol/SKILL.md
229|Doc adapters          → docs/agent-protocols/{codex,claude,grok}-heartbeat-adapter.md
230|```
231|
232|Declared reads/writes (a node may read anything in its own state; the constraints
233|below name what it MUST NOT write):
234|
235|- **Codex-worker** reads `{contract, status, rework_round, authority_epoch,
236|  worktree, comments_read_through}`; writes `{status, worktree, evidence refs,
237|  comments_read_through}`. Never writes `risk_tier` or `authority_epoch`.
238|- **Claude/Grok worker or reviewer** reads its stage/ticket state and upstream
239|  artifact paths; writes `{status (to waiting_review/waiting_hermes),
240|  comments_read_through}` and its own artifact. Never writes `risk_tier`,
241|  `authority_epoch`, or another node's files.
242|- **Claude-Router** reads typed state only; writes `{owner, status, route,
243|  authority_epoch}`. Never writes a verdict.
244|- **Hermes-Verifier** reads evidence; writes `{verdict, human_review routing}`.
245|  Never writes routing metadata or re-performs the router's dispatch.

247|## 4. Launch packet contract
248|
249|A launch packet is a node contract, not a mission briefing. Its contents are
250|capped to exactly four things:
251|
252|1. the ticket-state block (§2);
253|2. the immediate upstream artifact path(s);
254|3. the single handoff marker the node must emit;
255|4. the stop conditions.
256|
257|Explicitly forbidden in a launch packet:
258|
259|- full mission routes or DAGs;
260|- sibling-mission references ("LIP-01 and LIP-02 are logical siblings…");
261|- negative-space ticket lists ("do not touch these 6 unrelated tickets");
262|- pipeline role maps.
263|
264|Route topology lives ONLY in Kanban and in Claude-Router (§5). A node never
265|receives, and never needs, the shape of the graph beyond its own ticket and its
266|declared upstream artifacts.
267|
268|## 5. Routers: Claude-Router and Hermes-Verifier

271|families**, so dispatch latency is never coupled to review latency and the seat
272|that moves work can never grade its own dispatch (Decision D6 / ruling R1).
273|**Claude-Router** is the Main Orchestrator seat, held by Claude Code (Fable):
274|it launches everything and routes everything on typed state, and does no content
275|judgment. **Hermes-Verifier** is the independent verification + board-custody
276|seat, held by Hermes: it performs evidence review the router may never do, and it
277|owns the Kanban board. This is the same "may report/dispatch but may not do work"
278|separation already written for the 1-minute watcher, now applied across the
279|cockpit and along a model-family boundary.

{"output": "## 5. Routers: Claude-Router and Hermes-Verifier

Routing and verification are split into two named seats held by **different model
families**, so dispatch latency is never coupled to review latency and the seat
that moves work can never grade its own dispatch (Decision D6 / ruling R1).
**Claude-Router** is the Main Orchestrator seat, held by Claude Code (Fable):
it launches everything and routes everything on typed state, and does no content
judgment. **Hermes-Verifier** is the independent verification + board-custody
seat, held by Hermes: it performs evidence review the router may never do, and it
owns the Kanban board. This is the same "may report/dispatch but may not do work"
separation already written for the 1-minute watcher, now applied across the
cockpit and along a model-family boundary.

### 5.1 Claude-Router (dispatch — Main Orchestrator)

- **Seat:** the Main Orchestrator, held by Claude Code (Fable). It launches every
  agent and fleet, runs the One-Prompt Machine (mission intake H0), decomposes
  the mission, and routes everything on typed state. It holds no verification or
  board-mutation authority — those are Hermes-Verifier's (§5.2) — and it respects
  the model-law roster (`## Binding stage and coding law`) for worker assignment.
- Reads: the typed state block only (§2). Never replays full comment threads to
  decide a routing action.
- Does: picks the next edge from classified state; assigns `owner`; sets `status`;
  advances `authority_epoch` on authority handover; emits the route marker.
- Writes: `{owner, status, route, authority_epoch}` — routing metadata only.
- **Forbidden:** content judgment of any kind. The Router never decides whether a
  diff, artifact, or test passes. It consumes a Verifier verdict; it does not
  produce one. It never mutates the board's review state (that is board custody,
  §5.2).
- Write-permission set: `owner`, `status`, `route`, `authority_epoch`,
  `escalation_target`, and the routing markers `HERMES AUTHORIZED NEXT`,
  `HERMES AUTHORIZED ROUTE`, `WORKER CONTINUITY OVERRIDE`.

### 5.2 Hermes-Verifier (evidence review + board custody)

- **Seat:** the independent verification + board-custody seat, held by Hermes.
  Beyond evidence review it holds **Kanban board custody, Kanban board crafting,
  and Manual QA runs** (ruling R1) — the incident-hardened board machinery stays
  where it is proven, in a different model family from the Router.
- Reads: the completed artifact/diff, RED→GREEN evidence, tests, live product
  evidence, reviewer evidence, and applicable comments.
- Does: performs the stage/ticket evidence review that cannot be delegated away;
  crafts and custodies the Kanban board; runs Manual QA.
- Writes: a `verdict` field and, on pass, the human-review routing decision.
- The Router consumes the verdict; the Router never re-performs verification, and
  the Verifier never re-dispatches.
- **Board serving + ticket format (V order, 2026-08-15):** the Kanban board is
  served on **port 9119 — always 9119, never overridden in missions** (`hermes
  dashboard`), so every agent and human always knows where the board lives. Every
  ticket carries its assigned model in SQUARE BRACKETS at the start of the ticket
  title — e.g. `[codex@gpt-5.6-sol] eval-04-tagger`, `[hermes] stage verdict
  PROG-05`; unassigned tickets carry `[unassigned]`. The bracket tag is updated on
  every (re)assignment and must agree with the mission's `loop_ownership` map and
  the model-law roster; the assignee column duplicates it, but the title tag is
  the human-readable law. Board-crafting and board-fix packets must instruct the
  Verifier accordingly.
- Write-permission set: `verdict`, `human_review` routing, and the verdict markers
  `HERMES STAGE REVIEW PASS`, `HERMES STAGE REVIEW CHANGES REQUESTED`,
  `HERMES CHANGES REQUESTED`, `HERMES DONE`, `HERMES BLOCKED`,
  `READY FOR HUMAN REVIEW` / `V MANUAL QA PACKET`.

`risk_tier` is persisted and set once (§2). It selects the review path mechanically
— the Router does not exercise judgment about which path to use:

```text
risk_tier = low
  → Hermes-Verifier direct diff review → same-cycle HERMES DONE
risk_tier = medium
  → one independent reviewer (peer-review-first, §9) → Hermes-Verifier
risk_tier = high
  → full review diamond (§7) + product-truth gate + V acceptance
```

The high-risk floor (§9) can never be tiered down. At H6 the Router self-audits
that the persisted `risk_tier` exists and that the routed path matches the tier;
a mismatch is a `HERMES STEP 6 SELF-AUDIT` failure.", "exit_code": 0, "error": null}

### Review diamond (medium/high implementation tickets)

For low-risk tickets the proportional fast path stands: direct Hermes-Verifier
diff review, same-cycle `HERMES DONE`, no mandatory peer layer. For medium- and
high-risk implementation tickets, the serial double-gate is replaced by a review
DIAMOND fanned out from `READY FOR PEER REVIEW`:

- Medium risk (`risk_tier: medium`): 2 parallel reviewers with distinct lenses —
  (1) correctness/tests and (2) security/data-safety — each a different
  agent/session from the worker and from each other, each read-only.
- High risk (`risk_tier: high`): 3 parallel reviewers with distinct lenses —
  (1) correctness/tests, (2) security/data-safety, (3) product-truth (live
  app/API/DB/browser evidence) — each a different agent/session, each read-only.

Each lens reviewer reads only the ticket diff/artifact, its file contract, and
the RED/GREEN evidence; none reads another reviewer's verdict. Reviewers post
`PEER REVIEW APPROVED` or `PEER REVIEW CHANGES REQUESTED` with lens-tagged
findings.

Hermes-Verifier is the MERGE node. It re-checks DISAGREEMENTS ONLY instead of
re-verifying every dimension:

- All lenses APPROVED → Hermes-Verifier records one `READY FOR HERMES REVIEW`
  disposition and proceeds to the Hermes/human gate per contract.
- Any lens CHANGES REQUESTED → the unioned findings return to the same
  worker/session as one `HERMES CHANGES REQUESTED`; `rework_round` increments
  once for the round regardless of how many lenses objected.
- Lenses disagree on the same finding → Hermes-Verifier re-checks only that
  finding against the diff/evidence, records which lens it upheld with evidence,
  and issues one reconciled verdict; it does not re-verify the dimensions all
  reviewers already cleared.

The independent-review safety laws are preserved unchanged: no self-Done, the
worker never self-advances to Hermes, and no reviewer edits the change it
reviews. The diamond adds parallel diverse lenses; it never removes the
independent gate.

#### Adversarial reviewer prompt (default)

Every lens reviewer is dispatched with this default framing, prepended to its
lens-specific checklist:

```text
You are an independent adversarial reviewer. Your job is NOT to approve.
Actively try to break, refute, or falsify this work within your assigned lens
(<correctness/tests | security/data-safety | product-truth>). Construct the
inputs, states, or sequences that would make it fail. Confirm the evidence is
real product/runtime evidence, not workflow or scaffold evidence. If you are
unsure whether it holds, FAIL it and state exactly what proof would change your
verdict. Approve only when you have tried and failed to break it. You are
read-only: report findings, never edit the change.
```

surfaces a finding that cannot be resolved inside the current requirements — an
ambiguous or contradictory requirement, a scope gap, or a missing product
decision — Claude-Router routes ONE bounded question back to H0/REQUIREMENTS
rather than forcing the planner to guess. The return carries:

```text
ARCH→REQ RETURN:
- from stage:
- blocking question (single, bounded):
- why it cannot be resolved in-plan:
- options considered:
- rework_round: n of 3
```

Intake answers the single question (V is consulted only if the question is a
product/architecture/safety decision, via the V DECISIONS PACKET), then the plan
resumes at the returning stage with the same owner/session. Reopening intake for
an unbounded redesign is not this edge — that is a new mission.

When a QA-loop verifier (peer reviewer, review-diamond lens, or Hermes-Verifier)
